prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1041; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot. The insured's vehicle was struck while stationary, and the claimant reports a knee injury and is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time of the impact. The other driver's statement matches the account given to us, and scene photos are in the file.

Entry 3: Reviewed the vehicle damage photos. The damage is mostly consistent with the impact described, and the estimate has been sent for review. No earlier damage to the vehicle appears in our records or in the shop history provided. The driver is listed on the policy, and nothing suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 4: Attorney provided the medical summary. The knee injury fits the kind and force of the crash, and no prior injury to the same area is known. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.

Entry 5: Recorded a follow-up statement from the claimant. Some small details were added since the first report, but the core account of how the collision happened has stayed the same and lines up with the witnesses and photos.

Entry 6: Medical treatment has tapered and the file is nearing a settlement evaluation. All parties have confirmed the accident occurred as described, and the claim is being routed to the bodily injury and property damage teams for final review.
